Q4_CFR05.verdict: Yes. P18(a) under the completion rule matches BR-Q4 and remains a necessary condition of it.
Q4_CFR05.reasoning: BR-Q4.1 requires the existing completion rule for every gated run and for the race touch. For the race it requires a finished race, with the event window not a target; bindObservations exempts the race's minutes, so a finished race is never partial and a race not completed is excluded anyway. BR-Q4.3 requires every strength session executed in full (its sets) with ADVANCE or EARNED gates and usable logs. In the runtime, weeklyGates holds every PARTIAL gated or strength row, and raced() now requires a non-partial report. So '!partial' in executedBefore never asks more than the runtime's re-entry predicate does. P18(a) still ignores responses, logs, gates and the systemic rule, so it stays necessary only. COUNTED_RUN_ROLES still excludes the optional walk, recovery runs, shakeout and strides (BR-Q4.2) and keeps WALK_JOG (the disclosed BR-Q4.1 exception). P18(c) is unchanged.
Q4_CFR05.sensitivity: With the 1978cc4 runtime read by the candidate harness (mixprev), RT1o and RT1 are TRAINING_AFTER while P18a_RUN is false, so P18(a) would flag F02's shape. On the candidate both read P18a_RUN false and neither is TRAINING_AFTER. RWo is still flagged by P18(c) on the 1978cc4 runtime.
Q4_CFR05.limit: As a necessary condition, P18(a) cannot see SSCTR-P34R2-F01 (SY1: P18a_RUN true, OWN_RETURN). That is not a defect of CFR-05; it is the gap CFR2-04 addresses.

QRE-P34-03.reasoning: BR-Q1.4 binds the top-level OWN_RETURN row to carry ownReturn {class, days, startDate, endDate, reentered}. It says only that a break inside x's own stop keeps its own inner label. The implemented record (stopInOwnReturn, ownReturnOf) does that. A nested own return's class and days can be recomputed from the case facts by the same rules. PREREG-6 Δ16 already sends a NOT_EVALUABLE nested unit to the domain judge with the case package. Recording nested ownReturn details would improve explainability; that is for Chief, Product/UX and Data with Engineering, not a sporting requirement. Pinning the field by a test is engineering's (T30 now asserts it).

QRE-P34-05.disposition: ANSWERED: conformant with the binding text; accepted as a disclosed residual (SSCTR-P34R2-O02); not decided further.
QRE-P34-05.reasoning: BR-Q1.2(a) defines a live session as one with a prescription and not SKIPPED. BR-Q4.4 tests 'every sport the week plans' over live sessions. BR-Q4.5 keeps SKIPPED handling as it is. So a week whose every strength session the athlete marked unavailable plans running only, and its running alone can re-enter the athlete fully. My UK1 reproduces the QRE's reading on all three runtimes: TRAINING_AFTER, SHORT 4, strength back-squat 2x10 ESTABLISH and db lifts 1x10 ESTABLISH. The not-done comparator UK1n gives OWN_RETURN, 1x7/1x12 ESTABLISH. It is pre-existing (Phase 3.3) and identical on R7D-FREEZE-4. The mirror (UK2: run days marked unavailable, strength done) is also TRAINING_AFTER. Running is then bounded by the single-run ceiling, at EASY 15, EASY 15, LONG 15, the same running as the not-done comparator UK2n. In both, the skipped sport resumes from its executed history, classed by the later break alone. The earlier break becomes history for that sport, not its own return. This belongs to the family of SSCTR-P34-F04 (a sport untrained between the breaks is read less conservatively than its de facto lapse). It is bounded by the R6 re-establishment recipe and the single-run ceiling. Counting a sport whose sessions are all marked unavailable as 'planned' for the full re-entry test would change BR-Q4.4/BR-Q1.2(a): a new binding reading, not a recheck matter. Route it with the per-sport return-class question (NF-R7AB-1 / R40 family) to the Founder/PCG if wanted. No number.

QRE-P34-06.disposition: ANSWERED: conformant with BR-Q4.4; intended; no change.
QRE-P34-06.reasoning: BR-Q4.4 says verbatim: 'For full re-entry, every sport the week plans (any live session, optional included) must have re-entered through that week. A week whose running is only optional therefore re-enters strength alone, and running reads x's own return.' BR-Q4.2's 'never blocks' concerns a missed optional session in a week that has required sessions of that sport; it does not make an optional-only week a running re-entry, and BR-Q4.2 adds 'an executed one adds no re-entry evidence'. Code: required() needs a gated role or a race key, plans() includes every live session. So a post-event week of optional recovery runs plus strength is strength-only OWN_RETURN at most, which is conservative for running. The asymmetry the QRE notes (the same week with no runs planned would be a full re-entry) is the QRE-P34-05 family, disclosed with it.

findings.finding: When a named correction of the latest break moves its days, the report it supersedes still marks its old days as a known stop: unreportedBetween excludes every day inside a recorded return's interruption, and during the re-read that return is the one being corrected. Planned sessions the correction uncovers between the breaks are therefore neither asked about (TRAINING_BETWEEN_BREAKS) nor read as unknown. They count as missed. The corrected return then differs from the fresh report of the same facts, which asks first. In one shape the result is the restart the Founder's Phase 3.4 decision does not accept without justification. The Q7 ruling is explicit: a named correction supersedes only the report it corrects, and the stop is re-derived by the same rules as the first return, BR-Q1.2(c) included.

findings.cause: Code reading: unreportedBetween(ctx,from,through) drops sessions with date inside any episodesOf(ctx.program) live interruption. During recordedStop/stopOf for a named correction, the latest episode's live report is still the superseded one (the correction is not yet a decision), so its days mask. SSCTR-P34R-F01's fix excluded that episode only in appliedBetween.
findings.closure: On the re-read of a named correction of the latest break, the report it supersedes never makes a day a known stop. That holds in unreportedBetween and wherever the re-read reads recorded stops, with the same exception appliedBetween now applies. Planned sessions the correction uncovers with no report are asked, exactly as a fresh report asks. Expected: CU1 = CU1f (ASK, the Monday lift); CU3 = CU3f (ASK, the Sunday long run), and CU3 answered done = CU3fa (SHORT 4 OWN_RETURN); LC1 and LC1d ask about Mon-Tue wk6 as LC1f; CU2's question lists the five week-5 sessions as CU2f does (the R7-A date question may still follow, unchanged); C5, CU1d, CU3a, T21, T22, T26 and T28 unchanged.
